title: Evidence: Herman Miller Authenticity Concerns

attachments.platform_description:
Photo of the chair's label showing "Herman Miller" branding.
The label is printed on an adhesive sticker affixed to the frame, not embossed or stamped into the material.
The font weight and character spacing differ from the reference label shown on Herman Miller's current product pages.
attachments.title: Photo 1: Label Close-up

attachments.platform_description:
Side-by-side comparison: left shows the received chair's label, right shows Herman Miller's official label image from hermanhiller.com.
Differences in font weight and letter spacing are visible between the two labels.
attachments.title: Photo 2: Label Comparison

attachments.platform_description:
Close-up of the chair's mesh seat material showing the weave pattern.
The individual threads and gaps between them are visible to the naked eye at this zoom level.
attachments.title: Photo 3: Mesh Texture

attachments.platform_description:
Photo of the chair arm frame showing visible casting marks and seam lines.
Surface texture is unfinished in areas around the joint, with tooling marks and burrs present.
attachments.title: Photo 4: Frame Casting

submitted_text:
I've owned three authentic Aerons over the years. This one feels different.
The label discrepancy is the biggest concern - I've never seen a printed label on a real Herman Miller.
I believe this is a high-quality counterfeit, likely from overseas manufacturing.
